items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Luncford Luntswood was here at the time... they brought 5 or 6 musicians... I invited everybody from the clubs

ctx.x: So they brought 5 or 6 musicians; you know, Ben Webster and then came with Blanton, and Sonny Greer and Rex Stewart Stuart; they came in during the night, and I invited everybody from the clubs, but only performers and musicians could come. And the place was loaded; they came from the Belle Tavern, in Gardenia, there was a Belle Tavern in Gardenia, which I didn't tell you earlier ... there was a musician, he was a guitarist; his name was C.B. Burke; I think he wrote "When the Swallows Come Back to Capistrano" --…

But the big thing was that Lunceford Luntz was in town, and Duke was in town, because Duke was in town because he was doing downtown the show which ran quite a while. They got 5 or 6 men from each one of their bands, and then the trios would play, and then we would close it, you know. And naturally, it was kind of a mismatch, because we would burn them up -- because we had all these arrangements, you know, and they were from a big band and we were from a small band.

Then we went to Cafe Society -- and we stayed at Cafe Society I think for 3 months. Wait a second. No, I missed a point in there ... because before we went back to New York, Billy Berg had had another club, and that club was -- oh, incidentally, what I missed over at Billy Berg's -- Slim and Lemon Slam used to work there with us. I think that would be interesting to you.
